Rashi on Sukkah 44a:10:1.hebrew: ומי א"ר יוחנן - יסוד נביאים היא? והא הלכה למשה מסיני היא:
Rashi on Sukkah 44a:10:1.english: And did Rabbi Yoḥanan say - [That] it is an institution of the prophets? But isn't it a halakha transmitted to Moses from Sinai?

Rashi on Sukkah 44a:10:2.hebrew: שכחום - בגלות בבל שכחו את התורה והמצות במקצת, וזו נשכחה לגמרי:
Rashi on Sukkah 44a:10:2.english: They forgot them - In the Babylonian exile they forgot the Torah and the mitzvot in part, and this [one] was forgotten completely.

Rashi on Sukkah 44a:10:3.english: And they returned - The latter prophets.

Rashi on Sukkah 44a:10:4.english: And reinstituted them - According to the divine word.

Rashi on Sukkah 44a:11:1.hebrew: והא"ר יוחנן דלכון אמרי דלהון היא - רב כהנא היה מתלמידי רב, והיה חריף מאד, וברח לא"י לפני ר' יוחנן מחמת מרדין [שהרג לאדם אחד], כדאמרינן בפרק בתרא דב"ק (ד' קיז.). והוצרך לו ר' יוחנן לכמה ספיקות. והיה אומר ר' יוחנן לבני א"י: סבור הייתי שתורה שלכם, שלא גליתם מארצכם ולא היה לכם טירוף הדעת; אבל ראיתי שהיא של בני בבל, שאע"פ שגלו — עמדה להם חכמת החרש והמסגר שגלו עם יכניה, כדכתיב (מלכים ב כ״ד:ט״ז): הכל גבורים עושי מלחמה. ותניא בסדר עולם: וכי מה גבורה עושין בני אדם הנתונין בשלשלאות של ברזל? אלא שגבורים היו במלחמתה של תורה. אלמא ס"ל לר' יוחנן דלא נשתכחה תורה בגלות בבל:
Rashi on Sukkah 44a:11:1.english: And didn’t Rabbi Yoḥanan say: “I said [it was] yours; [in fact] it is theirs”? - Rav Kahana was of the disciples of Rav, and he was very sharp, and he fled to Eretz Yisrael before Rabbi Yoḥanan due to an incident of rebellion [for he had killed a certain man], as we say in the final chapter of Bava Kamma (117a). And Rabbi Yoḥanan needed him for several unresolved questions. And Rabbi Yoḥanan would say to the people of Eretz Yisrael: “I thought that the Torah was yours, since you were not exiled from your land and did not suffer confusion of the mind; but I saw that it belongs to the people of Babylonia, for even though they were exiled, the wisdom of the craftsmen and the smiths who were exiled with Jeconiah remained with them, as it is written (II Kings 24:16): ‘all men of valor, making war.’ And it is taught in Seder Olam: ‘And what valor do people bound in iron chains perform? Rather, they were men of valor in the battle of Torah.’ ” Evidently, Rabbi Yoḥanan holds that the Torah was not forgotten in the Babylonian exile.

Rashi on Sukkah 44a:1:1.hebrew: לדידהו נמי לא דחי - שלא לעשות ישראל אגודות אגודות, ונראה כשתי תורות, דלדידן לא דחי לולב שבת:
Rashi on Sukkah 44a:1:1.english: For them it also does not override [Shabbat] - So as not to make Israel [divided into] separate factions, and [lest] it appear like two Torot, since for us, [the] lulav does not override Shabbat.

Rashi on Sukkah 44a:2:1.hebrew: בגבולין - מוליכין לבית הכנסת. וכולהו בזמן הבית — דהוו כולהו בארץ וסמוכים להיות ב"ד, ויודעים אימת הוקבע החדש. אבל עתה, משחרב בית המקדש, אין לולב דוחה שבת, אפי' לבני א"י:
Rashi on Sukkah 44a:2:1.english: In the outlying areas - [This is where] they bring [their lulavim] to the synagogue. And both [teachings refer to] the time of the Temple, for they were all in the Land [of Israel] and close to the presence of the court, and knew when the [new] month was established. But now, since the Temple was destroyed, [the] lulav does not override Shabbat, even for the people of Eretz Yisrael.

Rashi on Sukkah 44a:3:1.hebrew: דלא עבדינן לה שבעה - אבל יום אחד מיהא עבדינן, כדאמרינן לקמן (עמוד ב) בר"א בר צדוק. והוא היה לאחר חורבן, שהיה ר' צדוק אביו בימי ר' יוחנן בן זכאי, ובימי ר"א ור' יהושע ור"ג היה, כדאמרינן בבכורות (ד' לו.): ״כלום חלקנו בין חבר לעם הארץ״, והוא היה השואל:
Rashi on Sukkah 44a:3:1.english: That we do not perform it seven [days] - But at least for one day we do perform [it], as we say below (44b) regarding Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok. And he lived after the Destruction [of the Temple], for Rabbi Tzadok, his father, was [alive] in the days of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai, and was [still alive] in the days of Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Yehoshua, and Rabban Gamliel, as we say in Bekhorot (36a): “Did we differentiate between a ḥaver and an am ha’aretz?”, and he was the questioner.

Rashi on Sukkah 44a:5:1.english: According to whom - In accordance with whose opinion did he say [that the] willow branch is rabbinic?

Rashi on Sukkah 44a:6:1.hebrew: עיקר - יום אחד מיהא יש לו שורש, אבל ערבה אין לה שום שורש מן התורה בגבולין:
Rashi on Sukkah 44a:6:1.english: A basis - For one day at least, it has a root; but the willow branch has no root at all from the Torah in the outlying areas.

Rashi on Sukkah 44a:7:1.hebrew: כהנים בעלי מומין - אף הם דוחקים ונכנסין להקיף ברגליהם וערבה בידם, וא"א להקיף שלא יכנסו בין האולם למזבח. וכל השנה אסורים ליכנס שם, כדאמרינן במסכת כלים בפרק ראשון:
Rashi on Sukkah 44a:7:1.english: Priests with blemishes - They too push their way in and enter to circle [the altar] on foot with a willow branch in their hand, and it is impossible to circle without entering between the Entrance Hall and the altar. And throughout the year they are forbidden to enter there, as we say in Tractate Kelim, in the first chapter.

Rashi on Sukkah 44a:7:2.hebrew: מי אמרה - השתא ס"ד דה"ק: מי אמרה שהיא חובה, וקאמר לצאת בה ידי חובה? ולהכי פריך: מאן אמרה, בתמיה:
Rashi on Sukkah 44a:7:2.english: Who stated it - At this point, it enters [the Gemara's] mind that this is what [Rabbi Yoḥanan] meant: Who said that it is an obligation, that [Reish Lakish] says to fulfill an obligation with it? And therefore [the Gemara] challenges: "Who stated it?!" in astonishment.

Rashi on Sukkah 44a:8:1.hebrew: מי אמרה בנטילה - ותהא חובת כהנים, דקאמר לצאת:
Rashi on Sukkah 44a:8:1.english: Who said [it is] by taking [it] - And [that] it should be an obligation upon the priests, such that he said "to fulfill [their obligation]"?

Rashi on Sukkah 44a:8:2.hebrew: דלמא בזקיפה - וכהן אחד זוקפה ע"י הכל, ואין חובה על כולם:
Rashi on Sukkah 44a:8:2.english: Perhaps by standing [it] upright - And one priest stands it upright on behalf of everyone, and there is no obligation upon all of them.

Rashi on Sukkah 44a:9:1.hebrew: יסוד נביאים הוא - תקנת נביאים אחרונים — חגי, זכריה ומלאכי — שהיו ממתקני תקנות ישראל באנשי כנסת הגדולה:
Rashi on Sukkah 44a:9:1.english: It is an ordinance of the prophets - An enactment of the latter prophets — Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi — who were among those who instituted enactments for Israel among the Men of the Great Assembly.

Rashi on Sukkah 44a:9:2.hebrew: מנהג - הנהיגו את העם, ולא תקנו להם. ונפקא מינה — דלא בעיא ברכה, דליכא למימר ״וצונו״, דאפילו בכלל ״לא תסור״ ליתא:
Rashi on Sukkah 44a:9:2.english: A custom - They accustomed the people [to it], but did not institute [it as an ordinance] for them. And the practical difference is that it does not require a blessing, for one cannot say "and commanded us," since it is not even included under [the injunction of] "You shall not deviate."

Tosafot on Sukkah 44a:1:1.hebrew: אמרי לדידהו נמי לא דחי - ל"ק מידי משופר, כדפרישנא לעיל:
Tosafot on Sukkah 44a:1:1.english: They say: For them it also does not override - [This] is not difficult at all from [the case of] the shofar, as we explained above.

Tosafot on Sukkah 44a:7:1.hebrew: כהנים בעלי מומים - ה"ה דהוה מצי למימר "ופרועי ראש", דתרוייהו אסירי אי לאו משום ערבה, כדתנן פ"ק דכלים (מ"ט): "בין האולם ולמזבח מקודש הימנו, שאין בעלי מומין ופרועי ראש נכנסים לשם":
Tosafot on Sukkah 44a:7:1.english: Priests with blemishes - The same applies, [such] that he could have said "and [priests with] overgrown hair," for both of them are forbidden [to enter there] were it not for [the mitzvah of] the willow branch, as we learned in the first chapter of Kelim (Mishnah 9): "Between the Entrance Hall and the altar is more sanctified than it, for [priests] with blemishes and [priests] with overgrown hair do not enter there."

Tosafot on Sukkah 44a:7:2.hebrew: אמר ליה ר' יוחנן מי אמרה - סלקא דעתיה דה"ק: "מי אמרה שהיא חובה דאורייתא, ואתיא ודחיא מעלות דרבנן? דלמא רבנן היא, דלא דחינן מעלות דרבנן משום תקנתא דרבנן!" ולכך פריך: "הא איהו אמרה!" ומשני: "מי אמרה שהיא בנטילה? דלמא בזקיפה!" וכיון דאין מקיפין את המזבח, ולא בעי אלא זקיפה בעלמא — אחד זוקף ע"י כולן. א"נ: בעלי מומין, אפשר להו לזקוף בשאר רוחות ולא יכנסו בין האולם ולמזבח. ואפי' תימצי לומר בנטילה, כדאסקינן לעיל דאיתותב מ"ד בזקיפה — "מי אמרה בבעלי מומין? דלמא אין הלכה למשה מסיני אלא בתמימין הראוין לעבודה, כמו שאין הלכה למשה מסיני בזרים אלא בכהנים, דבהא מודית, מדלא אמרת זרים נכנסין!" ולפי שיטה זו דפרי' דמעלה דרבנן היא — קשה לאבא שאול, דיליף (לעיל סוכה דף לד.) ערבה של מזבח מדכתיב "ערבי": אמאי בכהנים? דלמא אפי' בישראל, כמו ערבה דלולב! וי"ל: דשמא הקפת מזבח בכהנים, ושאר ישראל בעזרה בלא הקפה:
Tosafot on Sukkah 44a:7:2.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said to him: "Who stated it?" - It entered [the Gemara's] mind that this is what he was saying: "Who stated that it is a biblical obligation, such that it comes and overrides rabbinic stringencies? Perhaps it is rabbinic, [and] we do not override rabbinic stringencies on account of a rabbinic enactment!" And therefore [the Gemara] objected: "Didn't he himself state it?!" And [the Gemara] answers: "Who stated that it is [fulfilled] by taking [the willow]? Perhaps [it is fulfilled] by propping [it] upright!" And since they do not circle the altar, and nothing more than mere propping upright is required — one person props [it] upright on behalf of everyone. Alternatively: priests with blemishes, it is possible for them to prop [it] upright on the other sides [of the altar], and they would not [need to] enter between the Entrance Hall and the altar. And even if you want to say [it is fulfilled] by taking, as we concluded above (43b) where the one who said [it is fulfilled] by propping upright was refuted — "Who said [it applies] to priests with blemishes? Perhaps the halakha transmitted to Moses from Sinai was stated only with regard to unblemished [priests] who are fit for Temple service, just as the halakha transmitted to Moses from Sinai was not stated with regard to non-priests, but rather [only] with regard to priests — for regarding this you concede, since you did not say non-priests enter!" And according to this approach that we explained, that [the prohibition against entering between the Entrance Hall and the altar] is a rabbinic stringency — it is difficult according to Abba Shaul, who derives (above, Sukkah 34a) the willow of the altar from that which is written: "Willows [arvei]" — why [is it performed specifically] by priests? Perhaps [it is fulfilled] even by Israelites, just like the willow of the lulav! And one can say: perhaps circling the altar was performed by priests, whereas the rest of Israel [fulfilled the mitzva] in the Temple courtyard without circling [the altar].
